speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. To help you with your acute diarrhea, can you tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms and if there has been any fever or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection. Given the recent treatment with levofloxacin for community-acquired pneumonia, acute onset of watery diarrhea (≥9 episodes) with abdominal cramping in a 58-year-old female is highly suggestive of C. diff colitis. I will proceed with a C. difficile toxin assay and request a stool sample for analysis. REQUEST TEST: C_diff_toxin_assay.
